headline: Best week yet — subs 40 → 54 since Friday, 3,097 views on Nov 13 — with zero failures; one decision (captions) still waiting on you.
happened: Sun Nov 15 – Mon Nov 16: 6 single Shorts, 4 rapid-fires (two of them the new 7-sound variant, 49–52 s) and this week's long-form (Dragon-type, 6 min 28 s, first one voiced by Liam from the credit surplus). 29 workflow runs, 29 green.
Subscribers 54 (+14 in two days). Channel 54.2k views. Analytics (through Nov 13): 2,064 on Nov 12, 3,097 on Nov 13 — fifth straight day above 2,000. Instagram 121.7k views, 121 followers.
Public counts for the weekend's uploads: Shorts medians 486 (Fri), 579 (Sat); rapid-fires 424 / 517 / 539 / 572 — both formats at their highest sustained level.
The supervisor's Sunday run added two rapid-fire tests (coral vs Liam voice; think-time) and fixed a TTS edge case (a clip too short for its text is now retried instead of shipped).
ElevenLabs: 2,066 of 31,496 credits used, 23 days to reset — the long-form will keep getting Liam.

decisions.title: Reopen the captions decision? It was a tie on retention and static reaches 34 % fewer viewers.
decisions.why: The judge crowned static at the sample cap on a 3 % lead (bar is 10 %) and bypassed the views guard. The rule is fixed for future tests; this one needs a human call.
options: Reopen and keep kinetic as baseline (incumbent on a tie)
Leave static; carry kinetic's gold highlight and chunked Pokédex into static as a new test
decisions.recommendation: Reopen and keep kinetic as baseline (incumbent on a tie)
decisions.how: Reply in chat; it's a one-line edit to state/experiments.json.

ideas: Rapid-fire comments are now full guess lists ("1: blaziken line 2: dragonair 3: one of the hitmons…") — the score-tally opener could also count these partial-credit replies, not just "n/5".
"The typing helped so much" (Kanto Gyms rapid) is the first direct evidence for the silent type pills; worth a line in the rapid-fire description so mute viewers know to look for them.
watch: Cry test: original 73.8 vs modern 71.8 % viewed (n=14/16) — the two closest arms we've had; may end a tie, which now keeps modern.
CTA: score 75.3 vs subscribe 75.7 (n=6/7) — dead even on retention; the subs-per-video column will decide if either matters.
Series numbers 76.8 vs plain 76.5 (n=6/2), ladder 77.2 vs chip 75.8 (n=6/2), loop ending 60.8 vs spoken 57.2 (n=3/5) — all early.
GitHub dropped five hourly runs on Saturday; the watchdog now checks hourly and nothing was missed since.
